TO: All Managers
FROM: Deborah Kwan, Training and Development Manager
DATE: January 22
SUBJECT: New format for management training
Starting in March, the quarterly full-day workshops for managers will be replaced by a series of short online lessons. Each lesson can be viewed at any time from a work computer, so you will no longer need to set aside a full day.
This change follows the training survey that the Human Resources Department carried out in November, which drew replies from managers at each of our regional offices as well as at headquarters. Seventy-eight percent said a session of thirty minutes or less would suit them best, and sixty-one percent preferred to choose their own time for training rather than follow a fixed schedule.
I will admit the second figure was higher than I expected, so before the plan was finalized, I arranged short calls with managers from each office. Many explained that their busiest hours differ from those of other teams, and those conversations shaped our flexible approach.
Our in-house video team, which has made the company's orientation films for several years, is recording the first eight lessons now and will keep adding new ones each month. If there is a topic you would like the team to cover, please send it to me by February 12. Suggestions should concern the skills needed to lead a team, such as giving feedback or planning workloads.
Deborah Kwan

I am writing about a change that will affect your account. Starting March 16, we will handle client accounts through a set of industry groups instead of one shared account team. --[1]--.
Three years ago, we served 30 clients. That number has since grown to 64, and our 27 account staff members now often have to switch between different industries in a single day. Each group will focus on one kind of business and serve about 16 clients. Accounts for stores and consumer brands will go to the first group, restaurants and hotels to the second, health and fitness businesses to the third, and banks and law firms to the fourth. Miriam Voss

Birchwood Clothing to Open Largest Store Yet
Local clothing company leaves small shop for downtown space
By Colin Ashby
October 16
After eight years in a small shop near the train station, Birchwood Clothing will open its largest store yet at 140 Bayard Street on October 24. Founder Leticia Moyo said the larger space will also let the company host evening events.
The former bank building posed a challenge. Its main floor has only two small windows, and early plans left much of it too dark to show colors well. Architect Tomasz Weber worked with Dunmore Display Furniture to solve the problem by building lighting into the shelves and display cases. A Dunmore crew led by installation supervisor Rafael Ostrowski then put the pieces in place.
The new store will also be the first to carry a clothing line designed by Birchwood itself. The line's fabric comes from a textile maker based in the region that makes all of its cloth from recycled cotton. Ms. Moyo hopes the line will also appeal to Birchwood's online shoppers in more than twenty countries.

To: Ruth Okonkwo
From: Nathan Whitlock
Date: February 21
Subject: Spring Author Evenings
Dear Ms. Okonkwo,
Thank you for bringing so many of your members to our author readings last year. I am pleased to invite them to this spring's Author Evenings at Granby Public Library.
The series opens on April 3 with novelist Julian Frost, who will read from his new book. Poet Amina Farrow, who teaches at Granby Community College, follows on April 17. Signed copies of each author's books will be on sale every evening.
This season, registration cannot be done through our Web site, which will be unavailable until April while the library replaces its computer system. Instead, members may call 555-0151 or hand in a form at the front desk. All registrations must reach us by March 7.
Could you please share this message with your members?
Best regards,
Nathan Whitlock
Program Coordinator
Adult Services Department
----------------------
Granby Library News | Reader's Corner
An Evening I Still Talk About
By Leila Novak
I went to my first Author Evening last spring expecting a quiet talk. Instead, I found a full room and conversations that continued long after closing time.
The night I remember best was Julian Frost's reading from
The Harbor Clock
. He described his years as a newspaper reporter before he turned to fiction, and he patiently answered every question from the audience. Several of us bought the book that evening and discussed it for weeks.
I hear that a new season is already being planned, and I am looking forward to it.

To: Yusuf Akande
From: Brenda Kowalczyk
Date: February 3
Subject: Request for advice on reception uniforms
Dear Mr. Akande,
Stroud Legal Partners will open a second office in March, and we have hired eight receptionists for its front desk. As your company has supplied our uniforms for years, I would value your advice on which line would suit this team.
The receptionists will greet clients all day, so they must look neat. Our lobby gets warm in the afternoons, but that is a minor concern. More important, each person will wash his or her own uniforms at home, as we cannot pay for professional cleaning.
I look forward to your suggestion before I place the order.
Best regards,
Brenda Kowalczyk
Office Manager, Stroud Legal Partners
----------------------
To: Brenda Kowalczyk
From: Yusuf Akande
Date: February 5
Subject: RE: Request for advice on reception uniforms
Dear Ms. Kowalczyk,
Thank you for describing your new front-desk team.
Given the warm lobby, you might expect our lightweight NW-205 line to be the best choice. However, it must be dry-cleaned, which would not fit your arrangement. I recommend the NW-310 line instead. It was designed with exactly that kind of care in mind.
In my experience, three sets per person cover a working week. For eight receptionists, that comes to 24 sets, above the twenty-set level at which our volume price begins.
Our current catalog is attached for comparison. Once you decide, I will send a written quote and can bring sample jackets to your office for sizing.
Kind regards,
Yusuf Akande

To: All Staff
From: Diane Foley, Human Resources
Date: August 27
Subject: Staff retreat activities
Our annual staff retreat will be held at Cedar Lake Lodge on September 24. Each team will spend part of the day on a shared activity, and team leads should choose one of the following for their group by September 10.
Forest Trail Walk
: a two-hour guided walk on hilly paths
Canoeing
: paddling on the lake with trained instructors
Pottery Workshop
: shaping and painting bowls at tables in the art studio
Puzzle Hunt
: racing through the lodge's rooms and hallways to solve clues
Please submit your team's choice on the online sign-up form. Places in each activity are limited, so some activities may close early. Also note that canoeing depends on the weather. If conditions on the lake are unsafe, that group will join the Puzzle Hunt instead.
Diane Foley
Extension 3348
----------------------

On a separate note, thank you for choosing a venue so close to the office. Last year's long drive meant a very early start for most of us.
Best regards,
Simon Haugen
